In a Special Meeting of June 17, 1957, held at the Madison Public Library on Main Street in Madison Village, the Board of Trustees once again set a Public Hearing date to discuss the proposed Zoning Plan. In that June 17 th Special Meeting, Trustee Milton Nichols moved that the Trustees advertise that a hearing be held on the Zoning Resolution as approved by the Lake County Planning Commission and the Zoning Commission. The Public Hearing was to be held at Madison Memorial High School on Friday night July 19, 1957 at 8:00 p.m. The Township Clerk was also instructed to place copies of the proposed Zoning Resolution and Zoning Map in the Madison Public Library. THE HISTORY OF THE ADOPTION OF ZONING IN MADISON TOWNSHIP Ohio Townships were first granted the authority to adopt local Zoning regulations through legislation passed by the Ohio General Assembly in 1947. The first documented discussions regarding zoning in Madison Township occurred at the Board of Township Trustees meeting of March 24, 1951. At that March 24 th meeting, Township Trustees Dennis Smead, Eugene Miller and Jerome Emerson were presented with a petition from the “North Madison Improvement Association”. The group’s petition asked that the Trustees proceed under the requirements in the “ Ohio General Code ” for Township Zoning, and to adopt a plan of zoning only in the unincorporated area of Madison Township known by the Board of Elections of Lake County, Ohio as Precincts D & E.
